sentences.text: Eurazhdarcho is an extinct genus of pterosaur belonging to the azhdarchid family, found in Transylvania, Romania, within Upper Cretaceous deposits.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton that lacks a skull but includes three cervical vertebrae, the third and fourth metacarpals, parts of wing finger phalanges, and some indeterminate fragments.
The third cervical vertebra is unusually long, reaching three-quarters the length of the fourth vertebra, compared to the normal 60 percent found in other azhdarchids.
The prezygapophyses are well-developed and elongated, pointing obliquely forward and outward at a 30° angle relative to the vertebral axis.
Circular bite marks on the fossil were inflicted by a crocodyliform, providing evidence that the carcass was scavenged after death.
The discovery implies two distinct azhdarchid species lived in the Hațeg fauna: the gigantic Hatzegopteryx and the medium-sized Eurazhdarcho.
Pterosaur fossils were first unearthed in 2009 in the Sebeș Formation near Lancrăm by paleontologist Mátyás Vremir.
The genus and type species Eurazhdarcho langendorfensis were named in 2013 by Mátyás Vremir, Alexander Kellner, Darren Naish, and Gareth Dyke.
Comparisons with Zhejiangopterus suggest Eurazhdarcho had a wingspan of no more than 3 meters.
Researchers suggest Eurazhdarcho likely hunted small terrestrial prey on land rather than eating fish, based on the abundance of land animals in its habitat.
The presence of terrestrial fauna supports the superstork model, suggesting Eurazhdarcho was a terrestrial stalker that snatched prey while walking on all fours.
The fossil was later covered by a thin layer of mud and damaged by beetles and termites.
Eurazhdarcho was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae based on comparative anatomy, without a cladistic analysis.
A 2021 phylogenetic analysis by Brian Andres placed Eurazhdarcho in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as EME VP 312, dates to the upper Early Maastrichtian, approximately 69 million years ago.
Eurazhdarcho was found in the Upper Cretaceous on the Hateg Island, part of the ancient European archipelago.
Eurazhdarcho lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
A 2023 study by Rubi Pêgas and colleagues recovered Eurazhdarcho in a basal position within Azhdarchidae, clading it with Phosphatodraco, Wellnhopterus, and Aralazhdarcho.
The phylogenetic position of Eurazhdarcho within Azhdarchidae is debated, with studies placing it either in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae or in a basal position.
It is unclear how the coexistence of large and medium azhdarchids correlates with specific prey preferences or hunting techniques.
